body:
Hi woruteyqi,

Godot currently does not support reading the `whiteLuminance` attribute of the EXR file format, so this value is ignored and colour values will always be treated as relative luminance (relative to `window_get_hdr_output_current_reference_luminance` in HDR or relative to 100% white in SDR mode), rather than absolute luminance. Because the absolute luminance of SDR mode cannot be known, this behaviour in Godot ensures that SDR and HDR modes always behave consistently for values that can be represented in SDR mode and also for HDR values that can be presented in both modes through tonemapping. This is the foundation of the "Extended Dynamic Range" (EDR) paradigm that Godot uses that is also the primary approach used by a number of Godot's target platforms, such as macOS and iOS, and Android.

In practice, there are no platforms where we can guarantee absolute luminance values will be accurately presented to the user, due to brightness controls in devices with built-in HDR screens.

All that said, you can use `window_get_hdr_output_current_reference_luminance` to adjust the [`self_modulate`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_canvasitem.html#class-canvasitem-property-self-modulate) property as a best-attempt to control the actual luminance that your texture will be presented as. I would strongly recommend against hardcoding the Window's reference luminance in your project; this property is only available for certain platforms (Windows) and should only be adjusted by the player to adjust the HDR brightness of their game, rather than being hardcoded. Please read the docs for [`window_set_hdr_output_reference_luminance`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_displayserver.html#class-displayserver-method-window-set-hdr-output-reference-luminance) for more information on this.

You can read more about the HDR approach used by Godot on the [HDR output docs page](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/rendering/hdr_output.html).

I hope that makes sense, but if it doesn't: **the simple solution to your issue is to adjust your HDR EXR file so that RGB `(1.0, 1.0, 1.0)` in your EXR file is what you expect to be presented as 100% white in SDR mode.**

I can't reproduce any issues or unexpected behaviour using your MRP, so I'm going to close this for now, but please let us know if you still think there may be an issue after reading what I've written here.

> However, if the source image itself is already HDR content in linear space, it should not be subjected to this luminance adjustment via `reference_multiplier`.

Godot has been designed with the Extended Dynamic Range (EDR) paradigm, as described in [this video](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2021/10161/) and [the docs](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/rendering/hdr_output.html). With the EDR paradigm, HDR content **should** be subjected to luminance adjustment so that both SDR and HDR content share the same reference white luminance.

If you do not want to use the EDR paradigm, but instead want to control the reference white luminance directly in your project, you can set this directly using [`window_set_hdr_output_reference_luminance`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_displayserver.html#class-displayserver-method-window-set-hdr-output-reference-luminance) and expose the setting to the player. But this feature is only available on the Windows OS. By using this function to set the reference white luminance, the "[SDR Content Brightness](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/hardware/display-graphics/hdr-settings-in-windows#all-standard-dynamic-range-sdr-content-and-apps-appear-too-bright-or-too-dark-on-an-hdr-capable-display)" in Windows OS will be entirely ignored and you will get the behaviour that you are looking for. No engine modifications are needed.

Regarding your EXR file, as I mentioned before, the `whiteLuminance` of the EXR file is intentionally ignored by Godot because Godot has been designed around the EDR paradigm: This means that `1.0` in the EXR file must always map to the reference white luminance described by `window_get_hdr_output_current_reference_luminance` in HDR mode or 100% white in SDR mode.

If you believe that `1.0` in your EXR file is not correctly mapping to `window_get_hdr_output_current_reference_luminance` in HDR mode or 100% in SDR mode, please let us know because that would be a bug in the engine.

**One important note about your screenshots:** My suspicion is that your web browser is applying tonemapping to your EXR file before presenting it, as this is common behaviour for most web browsers and many other media players. This means that luminance values above what your display can present are being reduced to the range that your display can present. This may explain why you can see this detail in the EXR image on your web browser but not in Godot.

> So I owe you an apology. I misunderstood what you meant earlier, this is not an engine issue.

No problem! I am actually not very familiar with the WGC/DXGI behaviour, so it's good to know about the adjustments it applies. I appreciate you taking the time to test things thoroughly.

If you weren't aware, you can save an EXR file of a Godot `Window` by using the `Image.save_exr` function with the `color_image` parameter set to `true` and the `max_linear_value` parameter set to `window.get_output_max_linear_value()`. By using these two parameters you will get a result that matches the behaviour of the blit shader in Godot.

I wrote a bit more on this subject of capturing screenshots here: https://allenwp.com/blog/2026/04/30/how-to-save-hdr-screenshots-in-godot/
